description: How a particular case will run, step by step (O-5, DECISION-0052): a log of {date, attempt?, facts?} is executed frame by frame, and the law of each frame is the law of ITS date. The answer says: which stages have been entered; which attempted transition produced NO legal effect (§164 — "the act was performed but did not take place"); which duties are violated and which time limits are running; what is available next and WHAT EXACTLY is missing for the rest. The names of transitions come from law_process. Stages entered means "was it ever entered", not "where it is now": the core 0.1 does not compute points of the current state.

instance.description: what is going through the procedure: the number of the lot, of the application, of the case

legalTime.description: the base date (YYYY-MM-DD); the date of a frame is set by the step itself

probeTime.description: the instant of a hypothetical attempt, used to work out the steps available on the last frame; without it the available steps are not computed — the tool does not invent time

procedure.description: the procedure, where there is more than one

steps.description: the log of the case: [{date, attempt?, time?, decisionTime?, knowledgeTime?, facts: [{predicate, args}]}]; on an attempted transition `time` is the instant of the event (ISO 8601 with an offset), and by it the bearer takes its place in the history §161.1 (DECISION-0156); the decision and knowledge axes of a frame come from the entry, else from the case, else from midnight UTC of the date; every frame names the axes it used and where they came from

name: law_process_run
